issue.title: ob lock_wait_behavior intermittently fails with Contended under parallel cargo test
issue.description:
Reported by phase bead bob-cli-3s.4 (epic bob-cli-3s, a structural split of capture_clip that does not touch src/native/ob.rs) on 2026-10-03: during full-suite default-parallel `just all` / `cargo test` runs, `native::ob::tests::lock_wait_behavior` failed intermittently with a `Contended` lock error. It passed in isolation and sometimes under `--test-threads=4`. The fail rate was not measured; it appeared in at least one of several full-suite runs. The bob-cli-3s land run's own `just all` passed.

Suspected root cause (unconfirmed; the exact failing `expect` was not captured): `try_acquire_lock` uses an flock-style `try_lock_exclusive`, which belongs to the open file description. After the test's `drop(held)`, another lib test thread that is spawning a child process (many lib tests run `git` via `Command`) can still hold a fork-inherited duplicate of the lock fd until its `exec` closes it (CLOEXEC). During that window, the immediate `try_acquire_lock().expect("re-acquire lock")` sees `WouldBlock` and panics with `Contended`. The only `expect`s in this test that can surface `Contended` are "initial lock" and "re-acquire lock"; the waiter and zero-budget paths return `LockWaitError::Timeout` instead.

Check this before fixing. One option is to make the re-acquire tolerate a brief inherited-fd window (for example, `acquire_lock_waiting` with a short budget) without weakening the callback-count assertions. Do not serialize the whole suite.
